publisher: American Academy of Sleep Medicine / Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine
citation: Maski KP, Amos LB, Carter JC, Koch EE, Kazmi U, Rosen CL. Recommended protocols for the Multiple Sleep Latency Test and Maintenance of Wakefulness Test in children: guidance from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine. J Clin Sleep Med. 2024;20(4):631-641.
libraryFile: 2024 - Pediatric MSLT and MWT Protocols - Maski et al AASM.pdf
bestFor: Pediatric PSG-MSLT clinical and technical preparation, age-appropriate sleep scheduling, caregiver and developmental considerations, medication/substance planning, test conditions, acquisition, documentation, and reporting. The paper states there was insufficient evidence to specify a recommended pediatric MWT protocol and therefore focuses on MSLT.

mappingRationale.D1A: Supports pediatric clinical preparation and relevant sleep/medication context.
mappingRationale.D1B: Supports age-appropriate patient/caregiver preparation and communication context.
mappingRationale.D2A: Directly supports pediatric technical preparation, scheduling, acquisition readiness, and test conditions.
mappingRationale.D2B: Directly addresses technical staff administering pediatric PSG-MSLT and protocol execution.
mappingRationale.D3B: Supports pediatric daytime-test and preceding-PSG context while current AASM scoring rules control pediatric PSG event scoring.
mappingRationale.D3C: Includes acquisition, documentation, and reporting procedures relevant to report generation and verification.

authorityBoundary: Use instead of older pediatric MSLT procedural parameters where they differ. This source is a pediatric daytime-testing protocol, not a general pediatric PSG technical guideline; current AASM scoring rules control pediatric PSG scoring and facility/age-specific procedures remain necessary for local execution.
copyrightUse: Use article title, citation, section/box names, original summaries, and learning objectives. Avoid reproducing substantial protocol text, boxes, figures, or tables.
